narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and your credit history. Your checking account status had the greatest impact and pushed the decision firmly toward denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only about 13% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

Your credit history also worked against you, though with less force. The fact that all previous credits were paid back at this bank is rare; only 3% of approved applicants share this exact history. While it shows you eventually repaid, the model interpreted the pattern as less favorable than the “existing credits paid on time” profile that most successful applicants have.

The loan amount you requested worked in your favor. At 2,746 DM it was actually below the average requested by approved borrowers (about 3,020 DM), which slightly lowered your risk score. Unfortunately, this positive influence was not strong enough to overcome the negative effects from your account status and credit history.

You should focus on building a stronger checking-account balance and maintaining consistent, on-time payments across all accounts for at least the next 12–18 months. Once your profile shows more positive patterns, reapply or explore smaller loan amounts that better match typical approved requests.
